answer: Sybil resistance comes from tying every action to a priced, non-cloneable receipt. A new identity must survive a slow warm-up: each epoch its answer goes out as a pulse to five rotating peers it never invited, signatures sealed under a per-epoch cipher keyed to the requester, so a farm reusing one key cannot mint five distinct attestations. Clones are priced out too: self-recruited accounts earn zero graded work. Established peers act as a harbor for newcomers, staking reputation on each vouch, so a bad bet burns the voucher. Cheating costs more than mining honestly.
